issue.title: cronctl status should warn when an enrolled machine has no Postfix relayhost
issue.description:
## Feature proposal

`cronctl status` should warn when an enrolled machine's Postfix has no `relayhost`.

On 2026-11-10 the Mac's `/etc/postfix/main.cf` had no relay, so cron failure mail went straight to Gmail from `bbugyi@Kellys-MBP.localdomain`. Gmail rejected it with `550 5.7.26` (no SPF/DKIM). Bounces landed only in `/var/mail/bbugyi` on the Mac; `cronctl status mac` stayed silent. macOS upgrades can reset `/etc/postfix/main.cf`, so this can recur without a crontab diff.

Probe `postconf -n` for `relayhost` on each reachable enrolled machine (athena, apollo, mac). When it is empty, report a warning on that machine's status row (and in `--json`). Do not mail, do not mutate Postfix, and do not fail the status command solely for a missing relay.

## Why this is out of scope

The approved tale `plan:202611/finish_mac_cron_mail_relay.md` only restores the Mac's relay through athena, pins `HostName`, and documents the FDA reapply steps. Teaching `cronctl status` to notice a missing relay is a new cronctl feature in chezmoi `home/bin/executable_cronctl`, not part of that tale.

task_type_fields.proposal: cronctl status should warn when an enrolled machine's Postfix has no relayhost (postconf -n), because macOS upgrades can wipe /etc/postfix/main.cf and the resulting Gmail 550 5.7.26 bounces only reach the machine's local mailbox.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The finish_mac_cron_mail_relay tale only restores the Mac relay, pins HostName, and documents FDA reapply steps. A cronctl status warning is a new tool feature in chezmoi home/bin/executable_cronctl.

issue.creation_reason: The Mac lost its Postfix relayhost after a macOS reset, cron failure mail bounced locally with 550 5.7.26, and cronctl status never warned. File this so a later worker can add that status check.
